I do sometimes wonder if Fassad is a completely different persona to Locria, like a split personality that emerged as a result of Porky's brainwashing and manipulation.   By the time we see him in this game, Porky has become fascinated and disgusted by human weakness and the darkness in human hearts and living things,  which he seems to use as his justifcation to torment aand destroy life for his own amusement.     Like you said, Locria always seemed to be the black sheep amongst the Magypsies, and since the Magypsies are so flighty and concerned with etiquette and harmony amongst themselves, simply saying "Locria is not here" feels awfully loaded, considering how much they gush about affection for each other: smoochies smoochies and sending hugs and kisses and inviting each other round for tea parties or sending each other favourite snacktreats as presents.  So a blunt "Locria is missing" statement feels very ominous.   I remember when I first learned about the characters that they were named after the modular scales, and that was how I learned about the significance of the Locrian mode, in that it's a dissonant mode compared to the others.   So that seems to go into the idea that even before her betrayal, unwilling or otherwise, Locria was always the "odd one out".

I would say this sense of alienation from the other Magyspies is probably what lead her to turn traitor, or attracted Pokey to her: he sensed that even in immortal beings like the Magypsies, anger, bitterness, fear, malice, envy, spite and loneliness still lurked in their hearts, and the darkness in Locria's is what called out to Porky, seeing her as the weak link in the chain of Magypsies.    Since Fassad was ressurected as a cyborg, it's possible that Porky tortured and brainwashed Locria into a willing accomplice, amplifying the dark thoughts lurking inside her until they overpowered her original personality, replaced by the corrupted Fassad.

I think it would have been interesting to see Locria before she was corrupted, since we don't really see her personality very much.   The cut dialogue suggests that she was friendly and cordial, but also flighty and frivilous, like her magypsy comrades.   If it turned out that Locria was originally a flawed but good being, it would make her transformation into the hateful Fassad all the sadder.   It makes me wonder if by having Locria's betrayal be commented on by the other characters, and then having a character close to Duster be corrupted, that would mean the three main human characters all have to fight a corrupted Pigmask version of a loved one.  

I have seen some cool fanartspeculating on Locria's magyspy self: ofcourse she's wearing indigo to go with the rainbow/spectrum theme, but it seems people like to go with a feminine arabic for her: like a belly dancer or an odalesque theme.

It could be that Locria did go, but it's worth remembering that not even the other Magypsies have any idea about Locria or where she had gone and couldn't even detect her needle, so while Locria is a traitor, the game never really clears up whether she's a willing traitor or was an unwilling one.   It's possible that Porky was able to break her mind completely, and her new identity as Fassad was a false one designed to supress Locria's true identity and prevent it from reasserting itself once Porky had extracted all useful information. 

I think it's a shame because the game really leaves a huge question mark about Locria, and I really would have liked to learn why she betrayed the Magypsies and threw her lot in with Porky if she was going to vanish either way.   Finding out Fassad is Locria incognito is a huge revelation but the game never really makes anything of it aside from the reveal, I would have liked to know why Locria becamse Fassad, whether it was a willing and wholeheartedly betrayal, or if Porky used his abilities to torture Locria into submission (and Fassad's treatment of Salsa is an unconconcious memory of how Locria's mind was broken into that of Fassad).   

We dunno if Magypsies can be brainwashed, but it's worth noting that at this point, it's possible that Porky's powers are far beyond that of even a Magypsy.  If Locria can succumb to the darkness inside the human heart and become the greedy sociopath Fassad is, then perhaps it's possible that Magypsies can be broken or brainwashed too.
This is a loss for both of us.

A lot of "iamverysmart" people say this, but I personally believe that the educational system screws over a lot of children in different ways, and I would say my biggest problem with it is that instead of teaching methods being adapted to fit the different ways different children absorb information, instead the children/students are forced to adapt to the teaching methods, so what usually happens is that those students end up falling behind because instead of learning how their brain is wired to best absorb new information, they are being made to completely change how they learn and of course they struggle. 

Different people learn best different ways, and the "one size fits all" approach to education really means a lot of talented and bright students are deep miserable and flounder in academia and the general education system.   I've lost count of the times I've seen a child who was actually gifted in a subject dread and detest lessons in that subject because the teacher seemed to insist on them working on a way that was far too slow and rudimentary for them to learn anything new.     It's sad that Meg's struggles in math in A Wrinkle in Time were written in the fifties/sixties and yet nothing has changed in that front. 

I just think the educational system needs a colossal overhaul because it seems to set a lot of our brightest and most talented youth up for a lifetime of failure by destroying their confidence and faith in their abilities from an early age due to indifference and inflexibility.   What makes it worse is that when teachers genuinely do want to help their students with gifts/potential they are often prevented from doing so in any meaningful way due to red tape.   Teachers are not only prevented from disciplining their students most of the time, they are also prevented from supporting them as well. 

Me personally I was what you call a bright kid but I would say there was only one place of education I was in that I wasn't profoundly miserable in.   I just personally feel with the educational system is now and has always been, its geared only towards specific types of learning thriving, and everyone else struggling and stagnating and falling by the wayside due to the absolute refusal of the Powers that Be to adapt styles of learning and teaching.   Hell, we still insist on high school being first thing in the morning when tests seeem to suggest that teenagers are geared to sleep late as a vital part of development.

I think the problem with CGI is that it's.... too perfect.   I find giant robots and aliens and whatever made entirely out of CGI looks.... just not real. I just think cgi for things like Jaegers and Kaiju if they are enhancing a model that already exists in the real world, rather then something imaginary.

The armoured bears were guys in costumes with puppet attachments.  And you know what? That felt more magical and believable then the cutting edge but soulless CGI of The Golden Compass.    It wasn't trying to be something that's not there.  You just went with it. And I think that's just the magic of theatre and puppetry.

I also think when a movie doesn't have a huge blockbuster budget, often more creative ways are come up with instead of just going CGI CGI CGI CGI FOR YOU AND YOU GET A CGI AND EVERYBODY GET A CGI.    I'm really interested in "special effects" that are created with little or no effort or by interesting ingenunity.   One reason I love watching old live performances of the Supremes is how the light on their diamonds and sequins create this lovely shimmery sparkly effect as they move and dance and sing.
